zone_formula.description: Paces are offsets (s/km) from a reference pace. p10 = latest 10K time / 10. phm = Riegel half-marathon pace from that 10K: T10*(21.0975/10)^1.06/21.0975. goal_mp = goal marathon time / 42.195. Recompute after every checkpoint result.
zone_formula.note_v3: v3 uses the HM target directly for phm: 8640/21.0975 s/km; its p10 is the Riegel-equivalent 10K.

rules.long_run_spike: Warn if a run's distance exceeds 110% of the longest run in the previous 30 days (Frandsen et al. 2025, BJSM).
rules.easy_hr: On E/L runs heart rate is the primary target: flag if more than 20% of moving time is above the zone HR max.
rules.quality: On quality runs pace is primary; HR max is a ceiling. Cut a rep short if HR exceeds the zone max by >3 bpm or knee pain >3/10.
rules.knee: Knee pain ≤3/10 that settles by next morning → continue. >3/10, limping or worse next day → next run 30 min easy or rest. Two such entries within 14 days → show 'see a physiotherapist'.
rules.missed: Missed ≤3 days: continue as written. Missed a full week: repeat the previous week (shift plan by one week only if the user confirms). Never double up.
rules.fatigue: Easy-run HR 5+ bpm above the 4-week average for 7 days → suggest taking the next deload week early.

checkpoints.action: Race at the pace that kept HR < 165

glute_bridge.name: Glute bridge
glute_bridge.purpose: Wakes up the glutes before lifting or running.
how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat hip-width apart.
Push through your heels and lift your hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up.
Hold 1 s at the top, lower slowly.

lateral_walk.name: Banded lateral walk
lateral_walk.purpose: Activates the side-hip muscles (gluteus medius) that keep the knee tracking straight.
how: Mini band just above the knees or around the ankles.
Quarter-squat, feet hip-width.
Step sideways 10 steps, then back the other way.
cues: Keep tension on the band the whole time

goblet_squat.name: Goblet squat
goblet_squat.purpose: Teaches the squat pattern and builds quads and glutes, which protect the knee.
how: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest, elbows down.
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Sit down between your heels as deep as is pain-free, chest up.
Drive up through the whole foot.
cues: Elbows inside the knees at the bottom
goblet_squat.start: 8–12 kg for men new to lifting; choose a weight you could lift 10–12 times when 6–8 are prescribed
goblet_squat.progress: +2 kg when all sets are done at RPE 7 or easier; move to back squat in Base week B3 if form is solid

back_squat.name: Back squat
back_squat.purpose: Main lower-body strength lift for running economy and knee resilience.
how: Bar on the upper back (not the neck) in a rack at chest height.
Step back 2 steps, feet shoulder-width.
Brace your stomach, sit down and back to at least thighs parallel if pain-free.
Drive up, keeping chest and hips rising together.
cues: Big breath and brace before each rep
back_squat.start: Empty bar (20 kg) for 2 warm-up sets, then add 5–10 kg per set until RPE 7
back_squat.progress: +2.5–5 kg per week when all reps hit at target RPE

rdl.name: Romanian deadlift (RDL)
rdl.purpose: Strengthens hamstrings and glutes, the engine for uphill and late-race running.
how: Stand tall holding the bar at the hips, soft knees.
Push hips back, sliding the bar down the thighs, back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch (usually just below the knee).
Squeeze glutes to stand up.
rdl.progress: +2.5–5 kg when reps are smooth at target RPE

trap_bar_dl.name: Trap-bar deadlift
trap_bar_dl.purpose: Heavy whole-body pull that is easier on the back than a straight-bar deadlift.
how: Stand in the middle of the bar, feet hip-width.
Hinge and grip the handles, hips between knees and shoulders.
Brace, then push the floor away to stand tall.
Lower under control.
cues: Lock out with glutes, don't lean back
trap_bar_dl.progress: +5 kg when all sets are at target RPE

split_squat.name: Bulgarian split squat
split_squat.purpose: Single-leg strength and balance; trains each leg like running does.
how: Stand about 2 steps in front of a bench, rear foot laces-down on the bench.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is about parallel.
Push through the front heel to stand.
Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
cues: Most weight on the front leg
split_squat.start: Bodyweight for the first session, then 2×6–8 kg dumbbells
split_squat.progress: +2 kg per hand when all reps are at target RPE
split_squat.easier: Static split squat (back foot on floor) or step-up

step_up.name: Step-up
step_up.purpose: Knee-friendly single-leg strength; a good swap when split squats irritate the knee.
how: Put one whole foot on a box (knee about 90°).
Drive through that foot to stand on the box; the back leg only follows.
Lower slowly with the same leg.
cues: Don't push off the floor leg
step_up.progress: Add dumbbells, then a higher box

sl_rdl.name: Single-leg RDL
sl_rdl.purpose: Hamstring strength plus ankle and hip stability on one leg.
how: Stand on one leg, soft knee, weight in the opposite hand.
Hinge forward as the free leg goes straight back.
Stop when the torso is near parallel or balance breaks; return.
sl_rdl.start: Bodyweight, fingertips on a wall for balance

hip_thrust.name: Hip thrust
hip_thrust.purpose: Builds glute strength for hip extension and pelvic control late in long runs.
how: Upper back on a bench, bar across the hips with a pad.
Feet flat, shins vertical at the top.
Drive hips up to a straight line from knees to shoulders; pause 1 s; lower.
hip_thrust.progress: +5–10 kg when all reps are at target RPE

calf_standing.name: Standing calf raise (straight knee)
calf_standing.purpose: Strengthens the gastrocnemius and Achilles, which take several times body weight each running step.
how: Balls of feet on a step, heels hanging off.
Rise as high as possible, pause 1 s.
Lower for 3 s to a full stretch.
calf_standing.start: Bodyweight on both legs, then single-leg
calf_standing.progress: Single-leg holding a dumbbell; then machine with load

calf_seated.name: Seated calf raise (bent knee)
calf_seated.equipment: seated calf machine or bench + barbell/dumbbell on knees
calf_seated.purpose: Targets the soleus, the calf muscle that does most of the work in endurance running.
how: Sit with knees at 90°, balls of feet on a plate or step, weight on the knees.
Raise heels as high as possible, pause.
Lower slowly to a stretch.

hip_abduction.name: Hip abduction (cable or side-lying)
hip_abduction.purpose: Strengthens the side hip; hip work is part of evidence-based care for knee pain (patellofemoral pain).
how: Cable: ankle strap on the far leg, stand side-on, lift the leg out to the side 30–40°, slowly return.
Side-lying option: lie on your side, top leg straight and slightly back, lift with heel leading.
hip_abduction.start: Bodyweight side-lying or lightest cable plate
hip_abduction.progress: Add ankle weight or cable load
hip_abduction.harder: Heavier cable, 2 s hold at top

tibialis_raise.name: Tibialis raise
tibialis_raise.purpose: Strengthens the front of the shin for downhill running and shin-splint resistance.
how: Lean your back against a wall, heels about 30 cm from it.
Lift your toes as high as possible, keeping heels down.
Lower slowly.
tibialis_raise.harder: Tib bar or plate on feet

dead_bug.name: Dead bug
dead_bug.purpose: Teaches the core to stay stable while the arms and legs move, as in running.
how: Lie on your back, arms up, hips and knees at 90°.
Press the lower back gently into the floor.
Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg, exhale, return; switch sides.

side_plank.name: Side plank
side_plank.purpose: Strengthens the side core and hips that stop the pelvis dropping each stride.
how: Lie on your side, elbow under the shoulder.
Lift hips so ankles, hips and shoulders form a straight line.
Hold, breathing normally.
side_plank.start: Knees bent version if a full one can't be held 20 s

copenhagen.name: Copenhagen plank
copenhagen.purpose: Strengthens the inner thigh (adductors), which stabilise the knee and pelvis.
how: Side plank with your top leg resting on a bench (knee on the bench for the beginner version).
Lift your hips and the bottom leg so the body is straight.
Hold, then switch sides.
cues: Squeeze the top leg into the bench

pallof.name: Pallof press
pallof.purpose: Trains the trunk to resist twisting, which keeps running form tidy when tired.
how: Stand side-on to a cable at chest height, handle at your chest.
Brace, press the handle straight out, hold 2 s, return.
Finish reps, then face the other way.
cues: Don't let the cable rotate you
pallof.progress: Step further away or add load

foot_drills.name: Toe spreads + short-foot hold
foot_drills.purpose: Foot muscle strength and comfort with a bunion. Not a bunion correction.
how: Toe spreads: sitting barefoot, spread all toes as wide as possible, hold 3 s, relax.
Short foot: shorten the foot by gently lifting the arch without curling the toes; hold 10 s.
cues: Big toe stays on the floor

pogo.name: Pogo hops
pogo.purpose: Teaches stiff, springy ankles that return energy, which improves running economy.
how: Stand tall, small knee bend.
Bounce quickly on the balls of your feet, ankles doing the work, 2–5 cm off the floor.
Stay light and quiet.

a_skip.name: A-skip
a_skip.purpose: Running-form drill: knee lift, foot strike under the hip.
how: Skip forward, driving one knee to hip height while the other foot strikes down under the hip.
Swing arms in rhythm. Cover 20 m.

box_jump.name: Low box jump
box_jump.purpose: Builds explosive leg power with a soft landing (low impact because you step down).
how: Stand 30 cm from the box.
Swing arms, jump onto the box, land softly in a quarter-squat.
Stand up, then STEP down (don't jump down).

bounds.name: Bounding
bounds.purpose: Exaggerated running strides for power and elastic stiffness.
how: From a jog, push off powerfully into long, high strides, hang in the air, land under the hips.
20–30 m, walk back.
